# False positives

Taking a dataset, and randomly assigning groups should not produce meaningful
differences. Testing methods on this random assignment dataset should
not produce any significant results. If some are detected, that is a false
positive. 

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| output: false

library(mia)
library(bayestestR)
library(brms)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggsci)
library(tidybayes)  

options(mc.cores = 4)
```

```{r}
#| label: data-prep
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: Data preparation

data(Tito2024QMP, package = "mia")
tse <- Tito2024QMP

tse <- addAlpha(
    tse,
    assay.type = "counts",
    index = "shannon"
)

df <- as_tibble(colData(tse))

# Assign random group 
groups <- c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E")
df <- df %>%
    mutate(group = sample(groups, n(), replace = TRUE))

# Check means and group size
df %>%
    group_by(group) %>%
    summarise(
        mean_shanonn = mean(shannon),
        N = n()
        )
```

## Fitting models

As a baseline lets first do ANOVA, we should not get a significant result.

```{r}
res_aov <- aov(shannon ~ group, data = df)
summary(res_aov)
```

Indeed, no global significance. Against theory, we still do a post-hoc test.

```{r}
TukeyHSD(res_aov)
```

Even when trying our best to get a FP we dont. 

Lets try fitting a probabilistic model with `brms`.

```{r}
# Worst case, no pooling
formula = bf(
    shannon ~ 0 + group,
    sigma ~ 0 + group
)

formula2 = bf(
    shannon ~ (1|group),
    sigma ~ (1|group)
)

mod <- brm(
    formula = formula2,
    data = df,
    family = gaussian(),
    iter = 2e4,
    control = list(adapt_delta = 0.98)
)

# Posterior Predictive
pp_check(mod, ndraws = 50)
```

The no partial pooling model, only has regularization from priors. 
No shrinkage from a hierachical structure. 

```{r}
raw_means <- df %>%
    group_by(group) %>%
    summarise(mean = mean(shannon))
pop_mean <- df %>%
    summarise(mean = mean(shannon))
grid <- df %>% modelr::data_grid(group)
means <- grid %>%
    add_epred_draws(mod) %>%
    select(group, .draw, .epred)
preds <- grid %>%
    add_predicted_draws(mod) %>%
    select(group, .draw, .prediction)

plot1 <- df %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = shannon, y = group)) +
    stat_pointinterval(
        aes(x = .epred, y = group),
        data = means,
        .width = c(0.66, 0.95),
     ) +
    geom_point(
        aes(x = mean, y = group),
        data = raw_means,
        shape = 5,
        size = 6) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = pop_mean$mean, linetype = "dashed") +
    scale_color_brewer() +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
    labs(
        title = "Estimated group means",
        subtitle = "no pooling model",
        x = "Shannon Index",
        y = "Group",
        caption = "Fig1. Empty diamond indicates raw group mean. Point interval shows mean estimate with 0.66 and 0.95 CrI as thickened line."
    )

plot1
```

```{r}
## Helper function to gather summary table
pr_summary <- function(epreds, group) {
    names <- unique(epreds$group)
    cmbs <- t(combn(names, 2, simplify = TRUE))
    res <- tibble(
        Comparison = character(),
        Difference = double(),
        CrI.low = double(),
        CrI.high = double(),
        Pr = double()
    )
    for (i in 1:nrow(cmbs)) {
        comp <- paste(cmbs[i, 1], cmbs[i, 2], sep = " - ")
        draws1 <- epreds %>%
            filter(group %in% cmbs[i,1])
        draws2 <- epreds %>%
            filter(group %in% cmbs[i,2])
        diff <- draws1$.epred - draws2$.epred
        cri <- quantile(diff, probs = c(0.05, 0.95))
        res <- res %>%
            add_row(
                Comparison = comp,
                Difference = mean(diff),
                CrI.low = cri[1],
                CrI.high = cri[2], 
                Pr = bayestestR::p_direction(diff)$pd
            )
    }
    return(res)
}

knitr::kable(pr_summary(means, group), type = "pipes")
```
